operation_set._description: The complete set of operations an adopter overlay can perform against foundation state. It has exactly TWO members. There is no NULLIFY: foundation conventions are immutable-by-design for adopters, and an overlay cannot remove a foundation entry from the merged view. Retiring a foundation convention is a maintainer-side source edit; the `frontmatter.retired_types` tombstone is foundation-authored and overlay-extensible in the ADD direction only.
operation_set.add: Declare a key foundation does not declare (a new frontmatter type, a path_routing rule, a declared-union set member). No `_override_reason` is required — nothing is being shadowed. Declared-union leaves concat+dedup foundation-first per hooks/lib/merge-strategy-registry.json. For an array-of-object entity slot, an overlay entry whose registry-declared identity (`entity_identity_keys`) matches no foundation entry is likewise an ADD; when the foundation array is empty or the leaf is declared-union, every overlay entry is an ADD by construction.
operation_set.null_is_not_a_delete: A `null` overlay value does NOT delete the foundation entry. The merge primitive (jq recursive object-merge) has no delete, so a null merges as a KEY WITH NO CONTRACT — still present in `keys[]`, hence still ACCEPTED, while every required[]/tier read under it yields nothing. That is strictly worse than not attempting the override, so hooks/lib/foundation-overlay-load.sh REJECTS null-valued overlay entity entries before the merge (loud finding naming each path; the foundation entry stands) and hooks/pre-write-guard.sh independently filters null-contract types out of the union accepted-type set.
operation_set.supersede: Declare a FULL replacement value on a key foundation also declares, carrying per-entry `_override_reason`. For an array-of-object entity slot, SUPERSEDE is per ENTRY, matched on the registry-declared identity key (`entity_identity_keys` in hooks/lib/merge-strategy-registry.json): an overlay entry whose identity matches a foundation entry and whose value differs (compared with `_override_reason` removed) replaces that entry and owes `_override_reason` ON that entry; an identity-matched, value-identical restatement owes nothing; and because the merge primitive replaces arrays wholesale, omitting a foundation identity from the overlay array is an attempted REMOVAL — not a member of this operation set — which DENIES naming the omitted identity (restate the entry, or `--force-override` per write). This rule's DENY is what makes SUPERSEDE deliberate rather than accidental.

cross_cutting_meta_rules.rule_text: When adopter Layer-3 overlay and foundation canonical both declare the same rule ID or extensible entry kind: adopter Layer-3 SHADOWS foundation (adopter wins). Foundation declaration is preserved but does not fire. Adopter MUST carry `_override_reason` (free-text, mandatory) on every shadowing entry. Write-time DENY on shadowing writes without `_override_reason`; per-write `--force-override` bypass; no persistent disable. ARRAY-ENTRY IDENTITY: for an array-of-object entity slot, entry identity is the value of the slot's registry-declared identity key (`entity_identity_keys` in hooks/lib/merge-strategy-registry.json — e.g. doc_dependencies.entries keys on `id`), unique within each side's array by authoring contract (foundation) and adopter obligation (overlay). An overlay entry whose identity matches no foundation entry is an ADD; one whose identity matches a foundation entry with a DIFFERING value (compared with `_override_reason` removed) SUPERSEDES that entry and owes per-entry `_override_reason` on the entry itself (array entries are objects — the per-entry reason channel exists); an identity-matched, value-identical entry is a benign RESTATEMENT owing nothing. Because the merge primitive replaces arrays wholesale, an overlay array at a non-empty non-union slot that OMITS a foundation identity is removing that entry — removal is not in the operation set — and DENIES naming the omitted identity; the compliance path is restating the foundation entry (or `--force-override` per write). An array-of-object slot with NO declared identity key is FAIL-CLOSED: an overlay array over a non-empty non-union foundation array DENIES at the slot, naming the missing declaration.

_rules.failure_mode: A link to a non-existent target lands silently; the navigation graph carries a dangling edge that the reader only discovers on click — or an agent discovers on a failed file read. Advisory: write proceeds; operator told the broken target(s) per grammar + pointed at wikilink-repair (detection covers both grammars; repair proposals are wikilink-only) or to create the target file if intended.
_rules.rule_text: A file written with a link reference to a non-existent target SHOULD surface a write-time advisory naming the broken target(s), in BOTH grammars: wikilinks [[target]] / [[target|alias]] (vault-index resolution) and markdown links [text](relative-target) (resolved relative to the file being written; absolute/URL/anchor-only targets are out of scope). ADVISORY — never blocks the write; complements the post-hoc wikilink-repair capability, whose detection also covers both grammars. R-48 is the broken-link write-time advisory (Tier 1); each grammar gets its own advisory line.
_rules.source: governance/doc-dependencies.json :: _rules (SoT). R-48 is the broken-link Tier-1 advisory enforced at hooks/pre-write-guard.sh; declared here so it is visible to the rules-index.

_rules.rule_text: When an upstream document declared in this registry's entries[]/entities[] is edited, its declared downstream consumers/mirrors should be cascaded. ADVISORY — surfaced at write-time and at librarian session-close; never a write-time DENY. R-54 is the canonical doc-dep cascade ID; the hook header label is R-54 (renamed from R-07).

doc_dependencies.description: Documentation dependency registry. Hand-editable source of truth. Read by pre-write-guard.sh and librarian session-close. Mirrored into state/manifests/librarian-manifest.json -> doc_dependencies on each /librarian full run. Cascade registry consumed by pre-write-guard.sh + librarian session-close. The entities{} block is a declarative entity-mirror registry; per-type parity is enforced independently by trinity-drift-detect (plan) + memory-hygiene (memory); no generic entity-parity capability ships.

entities._comment: Entity parity registry. Each entity declares a canonical source path template with {name} placeholder, an instance-enumerator (glob/file-list/directory-index), the canonical field to compare, and mirrors with strict/presence-only flags. Declarative entity-mirror registry; per-type parity enforced independently by trinity-drift-detect (plan) + memory-hygiene (memory); no generic entity-parity capability ships.

considered_options.heading: Considered Options
considered_options.placement: between Context and Decision (the alternatives the Decision chose among)
considered_options.rationale: MADR's load-bearing thesis is that capturing the REJECTED options + their trade-offs is what makes a record valuable later. Required only on contested decisions; preserves the size_limits.max_lines 120 cap (long rationale stays in context-packets/ or the spec).
considered_options.required_when: the Decision had real contested alternatives (a genuine fork with more than one viable path)

section_semantics.Consequences: What becomes easier and what becomes harder as a result — including follow-on work, accepted trade-offs, and anything a superseding ADR would need to revisit.
section_semantics.Context: The forces at play — the situation, constraints, and tensions that make a decision necessary. Factual and neutral; does not state the decision.
section_semantics.Decision: The decision made, stated in active voice ('We will …'). One decision per ADR.

status_line.rationale: A single status token (or the concrete supersession form). The supersession form embeds the superseding ADR ordinal so the chain is human-readable; the manifest pointer carries the bare token + a separate superseded_by field.
status_line.value_enum_note: Status enum reconciled to the MADR-canonical {proposed, accepted, rejected, deprecated} + superseded-by-ADR-NN form, across the three coupled surfaces (this contract + governance/plans-rules.json :: decision_records.status_enum + schemas/plan-manifest-schema.json :: decision_records[].status) under R-37 documentary lockstep. MADR captures rejected options as first-class records.

adr.md.description: Hook-consumable runtime artifact for plan-tree Architecture Decision Records at <plan>/decisions/ADR-NN-<slug>.md. The k8s ValidatingAdmissionPolicy paramKind for the ADR record type. Decisions that would otherwise be buried in spec prose / context-packets / handoffs become short, immutable, individually-addressable, supersession-tracked records — the RFC→ADR best-practice borrow (Nygard ADR format). Matcher convention declared at governance/plans-rules.json :: decision_records; manifest pointer array at schemas/plan-manifest-schema.json :: decision_records[].
adr.md.filename_rationale: ADR-NN-<slug>.md — NN is a monotonic two-digit (or wider) creation-order ordinal within the plan's decisions/ dir; slug is a short kebab-case decision name. Ordinal is immutable once published (like task IDs).
adr.md.immutable_rationale: An accepted ADR is an immutable record of a decision made at a point in time. A decision change does NOT edit the original — it creates a NEW ADR that supersedes the prior one (the prior ADR's Status flips to `superseded-by-ADR-NN`; the new ADR references what it supersedes in Context). Mirrors the RFC→ADR supersession chain; distinct from the in-place amendment pattern used by spec.md.

size_limits.rationale: ADRs are short by design — one decision, the forces behind it, and its consequences. Long rationale belongs in context-packets/ or the spec; the ADR is the durable record, not the working material.

supersession.mechanism: new ADR supersedes old; old ADR Status → `superseded-by-ADR-NN`; new ADR names the superseded ADR in its Context

Enforcement fires at BOTH layers: write-time on REGISTERED-spoke Work/ writes — the pre-write-guard.sh remap prelude rewrites a registered Work/<spoke>/ write onto the vault path BEFORE the 3-tier schema block, so the write IS governed — with the librarian suite over the Work/ symlink view as the audit-time backstop for everything else (unregistered spokes, hand-authored files reached via the scoped symlink walk). A deliverable is never machine-written. Those generated surfaces are NOT deliverables and are out of this contract's scope; they are disjoint from the deliverable class, so the never-machine-written boundary for human/agent-authored deliverables is unchanged.

h1.rationale: The single top-level heading names the durable concept the article carries; the file basename mirrors this concept name, so a cross-reference in either grammar (a markdown link's visible text, or a bare wikilink resolving by basename) reads as the concept.

in_document_toc.rationale: An in-doc table of contents is permitted only when the article exceeds the soft budget and is not decomposable, and it is authored by hand, never auto-generated.

leading_section_index.rationale: A leading in-document section index is forbidden; the article is short enough that a reader scans the body directly, and an auto-generated index drifts from hand-edited prose.

sibling_wikilinks_at_foot.placement: at the foot of the body
sibling_wikilinks_at_foot.rationale: Sibling articles are cross-referenced at the foot for backlink-graph value. The corpus addressing convention rules relative-path markdown links the target grammar (a real path resolves for an agent with no basename index); the bare-wikilink form remains accepted during the corpus conversion, backed by basename uniqueness and the basename-collision scan.

synthesized_body.rationale: The body is synthesized at promotion and scrubbed of all plan/project-specific detail (task IDs, plan slugs, engagement names, decision dates); it is regenerated content, not hand-maintained prose, so per-article changelogs are replaced by the single global library log.

library-article.md.description: Hook-and-scan-consumable runtime artifact for durable universal-knowledge library articles at _library/<topic>/<article>.md — one concept per file, synthesized by the librarian at promotion and scrubbed of all plan/project-specific detail. The k8s ValidatingAdmissionPolicy paramKind for the library-article type. This contract is the canonical home for the article's size_limits and the routing activation-condition field that the library-index scan reads as the first source for index Description columns. The frontmatter type registration (type: reference) lives in governance/frontmatter-rules.json#types.reference; this contract carries the WHAT-it-contains body-structure and the length governance.

revalidation_interval_days.guidance: Per-article staleness-velocity tier. Fast-moving tool documentation revalidates near 45 days; stable concepts near 270; the freshness scan applies a 90-day fallback when the field is undeclared.
revalidation_interval_days.revalidation_interval_days_rationale: Different knowledge ages at different rates, so a single global staleness window either nags on durable concepts or lets fast-moving tool docs rot; a per-article tier with a safe default keeps the freshness signal trustworthy.

routing.description: Activation-condition one-liner ('when to read this'): a precise scope/applicability statement synthesized at promotion. The FIRST source the index Description-derivation chain reads, ahead of description / H1 / first-paragraph.
routing.routing_rationale: A net-new activation-condition field, carried by no other shipped contract; it lets an index row state when a reader should open the article rather than restating its title, which is what makes a coverage signal load-bearing at research time.

size_limits.enforcement_detail: Length is enforced by the librarian library-index re-derive scan, which emits an over-threshold finding when an article exceeds the soft budget — NEVER by a write-time guard. No write-time body-structure or line-count guard governs library articles in the runtime.
size_limits.size_limits_rationale: A soft budget keeps each article one readable concept and an audit-time scan flags overflow without a write-time block, so a long synthesis is never silently truncated and the author decides between splitting and adding a manual table of contents.
size_limits.split_vs_pointer_rule: An article over the soft budget that is MECE-decomposable is split into per-sub-topic articles; one over the soft budget that is a single-topic narrative gains an in-doc table of contents above the body (never auto-generated).

frontmatter._description: Claude-consumed JSON registry for the frontmatter pillar. Loaded by pre-write-guard.sh at runtime and read by the librarian frontmatter-coverage-audit. Carries R-32, R-33, R-37, R-39, R-40, R-64 plus the type registry, tier compliance, path-routing rules, and the universal typed cohort + property_types value-typing declarations. Frontmatter is the API every file exposes to the system; this pillar declares the fields, per-type contracts, AND the rules that enforce them. The former schemas/vault-schema.json was dissolved into this pillar (types + tier assignment + path routing) plus governance/tagging-rules.json (tag-prefix taxonomy).

absorbed_from_vault_schema: types (were top-level type keys in vault-schema.json)
_design_notes.consumer: pre-write-guard.sh — SCHEMA_KEY case statement + R-32 type-allowlist DENY + R-33 placement advisory (reads .types[].expected_path); post-write-verify.sh — R-39 provides-presence advisory (reads .types[].canonical_scope); librarian frontmatter-coverage-audit (R-39, R-40)
_design_notes.evolution_protocol: R-37 atomic lockstep — frontmatter-rules.json + pre-write-guard.sh SCHEMA_KEY case + post-write-verify.sh type_map updated in one commit. NOTE: schemas/vault-schema.json was DISSOLVED into this pillar + governance/tagging-rules.json; the dissolved file no longer ships — author against this pillar and governance/tagging-rules.json only.

enforcement_layer: governance/frontmatter-rules.json `types` (type allowlist + per-type required/optional field declarations)
_rules.failure_mode: Files written with an unknown `type:` value or with missing Strict-tier required fields drift the schema contract silently. Downstream consumers (auto-routing, librarian, scaffold) cannot reason about the file because the contract has been violated. Without write-time DENY, the schema becomes documentation rather than enforcement — production-scale untagged-file backlogs (~500 files observed in a reference deployment) accumulate before audit catches up. The Tier 2 DENY closes the gap at the moment of capture, returning a structured error that enumerates the missing fields and points to the schema entry.
_rules.retired_types_handling: Files declaring a retired `type:` value (currently `engagement`, `project`, `system-governance-spoke`) are DENIED with the retirement reference and per-type `replacement` guidance. For `engagement` and `project` the replacement points the author to the folder-lineage convention (field-level propagation via `engagement:` / `project:` frontmatter fields); `system-governance-spoke` retires with no replacement type (the file is now plain user content). See `retired_types` block.
_rules.rule_text: Every Strict-tier vault write MUST declare a `type:` value drawn from the governance/frontmatter-rules.json `types` allowlist (retired types preserved in `retired_types`). For Strict-tier files, the universal required fields (`type`, `tags`, `updated`) AND the per-type `required` field list MUST all be present in the YAML frontmatter. Pre-write-guard DENIES writes failing either check; the DENY message enumerates the missing fields plus the pillar entry path. Adding a new type or extending a required-field list requires R-37 atomic lockstep updating this pillar + pre-write-guard SCHEMA_KEY case + post-write-verify type_map in one commit. Standard-tier writes emit a warning instead of DENY (operator triages via librarian frontmatter-coverage-audit); Minimal-tier writes proceed without validation.

enforcement_layer: pre-write-guard.sh folder-placement advisory branch (Tier 1; never blocks)
_rules.failure_mode: Files written outside the canonical folder for their declared `type:` produce structural drift that compounds — the file is invisible to type-scoped queries, lives in a folder that does not match its archetype, and creates the impression that 'this type lives anywhere.' Once the precedent lands, follow-on writes drift further. The Tier 1 advisory fires at write-time rather than waiting for weekly audit so the operator sees the misplacement at the moment of capture and can move the file before publishing wikilinks.
_rules.rule_text: Files declaring a `type:` value SHOULD reside under the canonical folder for that type per governance/frontmatter-rules.json `path_routing` (the per-archetype lineage rules). Pre-write-guard emits a Tier 1 advisory `[R-33 FOLDER PLACEMENT]` when the file's path does not match the type's expected folder pattern. The advisory never blocks — engagement-specific exceptions, cross-engagement reference docs, and adopter-customized folder structures are legitimate causes for divergence. The advisory text enumerates the expected folder pattern and the current path so the author can decide. Persistent advisory firings on the same type/folder pair surface as `placement-drift` findings in the librarian audit.

_rules._enforcement_layer_note: R-37 is documentary, not write-time-enforced. There is no `pre-write-guard.sh atomic-lockstep branch (DENY on partial-surface writes)` — PreToolUse sees one file per invocation and cannot inspect a multi-file commit set; and no `git pre-commit hook` ships with the foundation. Enforcement is git's commit-boundary atomicity (commits are atomic by construction) + author discipline at the close-out merge boundary + the librarian governance-parity-audit at audit-time.
coupled_surfaces: governance/foundation-master.json (forward; built from this pillar via tools/build-foundation-master.sh)
_rules.failure_mode: Schema-touching changes that land in one surface without the others produce silent drift — the pillar declares a new type the hook does not recognize; the rule registry references a field name the pillar spells differently. Within weeks the surfaces diverge enough that no single artifact is authoritative. Drift is detectable but already-broken when the audit surfaces it. R-37's structural commitment is that partial-surface commits are treated as the error they are; the close-out merge boundary and the librarian audit are the regression checks that catch drift before it ossifies.
_rules.rule_text: The frontmatter pillar binds two coupled surfaces under R-37 atomic lockstep: (1) governance/frontmatter-rules.json (canonical pillar declaring types, tiers, path-routing rules, and rule registry; absorbed the former schemas/vault-schema.json), (2) hooks/pre-write-guard.sh SCHEMA_KEY case-statement + hooks/post-write-verify.sh type_map (runtime mirror). Adding, modifying, or retiring a `type:` value, changing a required-field list, introducing a new field class, or updating the tier-compliance contract requires touching BOTH surfaces in a single commit. R-37 is documentary — enforced via author discipline at the close-out merge boundary, git's commit-boundary atomicity, and the librarian governance-parity-audit at audit-time. There is no write-time hook branch that denies partial-surface commits (PreToolUse architecture sees one file per invocation and has no view of the multi-file commit set; the proper enforcement layer for that would be a pre-commit or post-merge audit, not pre-write-guard). This entry is the pillar-scoped instantiation of the canonical R-37 meta-rule at governance/_index.json `cross_cutting_meta_rules[]`. The coupled-surfaces declaration in governance/_index.json carries governance/foundation-master.json (forward).

enforcement_layer: post-write-verify.sh provides-presence advisory (Tier 1; combined with R-38 blockquote-summary block)
exemptions: Archive/** — archived content; provides-declaration is structurally unnecessary
Daily/** — daily notes are temporally-scoped, not capability-scoped
Inbox/** — aggregation surfaces; provides lives at the canonical destination, not the staging copy
_rules.failure_mode: Long-form files (>200 lines) without a `provides:` declaration become opaque to consumers that route by capability rather than by path. The router cannot determine what concepts the file is canonical for; the librarian cannot detect provides-canonicality drift (R-40) because there is no claim to compare against; downstream agents loading the file have no fast way to decide whether the content is relevant. The advisory surfaces the omission at write-time so the author either declares `provides:` deliberately or accepts the file as content-only.
_rules.rule_text: Files exceeding 200 lines SHOULD declare a `provides:` array in their YAML frontmatter enumerating the concepts, rules, or capabilities the file is the canonical source for. Post-write-verify emits a Tier 1 advisory `[R-39 PROVIDES PRESENCE]` when a file over the line threshold lacks `provides:` or has `provides: []`. The advisory never blocks — content-only long-form files (raw transcripts, archive imports, daily-note dumps) are legitimate and the author can ignore the advisory. The librarian frontmatter-coverage-audit tracks recurring R-39 firings as `provides-coverage-drift` findings so the operator can triage at session-close.

_exemption_classes._description: Foundation declares the EXEMPTION CLASS shape; concrete adopter folder names (engagement-scoped subfolders, project-scoped subfolders, archetype-cluster subfolders, etc.) live in overlay-master.frontmatter.canonical_scope_exemptions[]. Foundation governance stays archetype-agnostic.

classes.name: instance-scoped
classes.rationale: files inside an archetype-cluster instance (engagement / topic / repo / etc.) are scoped to that instance, not vault-wide canonical

classes.name: sub-cluster-scoped
classes.rationale: files inside an archetype's sub-cluster (project / study / epic / etc.) carry sub-cluster-scoped `provides:` vocabulary, not vault-wide canonical

enforcement_layer: drift-allowlist override at hooks/drift-allowlist.json (`provides_overlap[]` for deliberate co-canonical pairs)
_rules.failure_mode: Two or more canonical-scope files claiming the same `provides:` capability fragment authority. A consumer routing to the capability does not know which file to read; updates to one canonical do not propagate to the other; the two files drift into mutually-contradictory statements within months. Without an audit, the drift is invisible — `grep provides:` returns both files and the consumer picks one by accident. The librarian-audit finding surfaces the collision and asks the operator to either consolidate, archive one source, or register the overlap as deliberate in the drift-allowlist.
_rules.rule_text: Within the canonical-scope of the vault (vault root depth-1 + Skills/**), no two files SHOULD declare the same capability in their `provides:` array. The librarian frontmatter-coverage-audit walks every Standard- and Strict-tier file's `provides:` declaration, builds an inverted index, and emits a `provides-canonicality-drift` finding whenever a capability is claimed by 2+ canonical-scope owners. Severity is `blocking` when any owner sits at vault root; `warning` otherwise. Engagement reference docs, meeting notes, project context files, and daily notes are EXCLUDED from canonical-scope — `provides:` is project-scoped vocabulary there, not vault-wide canonical. Deliberate co-canonical pairs (e.g., a research packet plus its consumer-rendered spoke) register at hooks/drift-allowlist.json `provides_overlap[].capability` with rationale + audit-trail entry; allowlist entries mirror into librarian-manifest.json on every run and suppress the finding.
scope_exemptions: Daily/** — daily notes are temporally-scoped (foundation-shipped folder)

enforcement_layer: pre-write-guard.sh property-type format-regex branch (Tier 1 advisory; warn-not-DENY under the shipped default)
_rules.failure_mode: Cohort fields written with a malformed value type — a free-text `created`, a scalar `tags`, a spaced `id`, a non-integer `schema_version` — are syntactically present but semantically unusable: date-range queries, list membership, slug reconciliation, and schema-version migrations all silently misfire. Obsidian Bases, an MCP server over the vault, and a RAG/GraphRAG exporter read the raw frontmatter and inherit the malformed value. Without a write-time typing signal the drift is invisible until a downstream consumer breaks. The Tier 1 advisory surfaces the type mismatch at the moment of capture so the author can correct the shape; it never blocks — the value is present, only mis-typed.
_rules.rule_text: Cohort fields declared in governance/frontmatter-rules.json `property_types` MUST carry their declared value type: `created`/`updated` a `date` (^YYYY-MM-DD), `tags` a `list` (YAML sequence), `id` a `slug-string` (^[a-z0-9]+(-[a-z0-9]+)*$), `schema_version` an `int` (^[0-9]+$). Pre-write-guard emits a Tier 1 advisory `[R-64 PROPERTY TYPE]` when a present cohort value does not match its declared type; the advisory never blocks (warn is the shipped default; per-vault hard-DENY is an opt-in override). The new cohort fields (`description`/`created`/`id`/`schema_version`) join `updated` in the soft-tier non-block set — a missing cohort field warns, it does not DENY. The enforceable typing layer is this write-time format regex; the seeded `.obsidian/types.json` is a UX-only mirror (brain-stem cannot enforce Obsidian's own property types). Adding or changing a `property_types` declaration requires R-37 atomic lockstep with the pre-write-guard.sh typing branch.

cohort._description: The universal typed frontmatter cohort applied to durable in-folder notes. Scope is LOCATION-BASED: every file resident in (or symlinked into, e.g. Work/) the brain folder (vault root) is in scope; machine files parked outside the brain folder (logs, XDG state) are exempt by location, not by type. The per-type required[] lists are the real enforcement surface; universal_required (tier_compliance) is documentary. Value-typing is the write-time property_types format regex (R-64).
cohort.exempt: out-of-folder machine files (logs, XDG state); memory files (memory-auto-stamp.sh stamps created=today, so the cohort/git-date backfill would collide)

parent_plan.disposition: Deferred from v1. Re-visit when planning methodology generalizes for adopters.
parent_plan.do_not: Do NOT add `parent_plan` to any type entry in this pillar. Plan-tree files validate against plans-schema.json + plan-manifest-schema.json separately.
parent_plan.reason: Plan-tree-only field; lives in plans-schema.json + plan-manifest-schema.json, not vault content governance.

CLAUDE.rationale: The vault-root instruction file is matched by exact path and carries no `type:` frontmatter for a `types` entry to key on. NO pillar or schema matcher governs it: the only runtime handling is the vault-root write class in hooks/pre-write-guard.sh, which knows CLAUDE.md as the sole mandatory vault-root file and exempts it from the propose-and-validate prompt every OTHER new vault-root file gets. Its contract's required_sections + size_limits + prohibited_sections are documentary — none is a frontmatter required-field matter, no write-time guard consumes them, and post-write-verify.sh skips the file; the shape is carried by templates/vault-claude-md-template.md and rendered at onboard time by skills/onboarder.

file_type_contract_dispositions._description: Closed-world reconciliation between governance/file-type-contracts/<key>.md.json and this pillar's `types` registry. `types` is keyed by the `type:` FRONTMATTER VALUE and drives the R-32 vault-write allowlist + per-type required-field DENY, whose scope is vault-resident markdown. A file-type CONTRACT is keyed by FILE SHAPE and matched by PATH (`applies_to.path_glob`). The two key spaces are not the same set, so a contract key absent from `types` is not automatically a gap — but it must not be SILENTLY absent either. Every contract key that is not a `types` entry carries an explicit disposition here, so the reconciliation is closed-world and machine-checkable: `path-governed` (the governed file is not a vault-resident `type:`-declaring note, so a `types` entry would be inert for the real file AND would newly gate unrelated vault files declaring that value; its `governed_by` names the surface that ACTUALLY handles the file — a pillar/schema that matches it by path, or, where no pillar/schema matcher exists at all, the runtime consumer that reads the contract) or `registered-alias` (the contract governs a type that IS registered in `types` under a different key). `governed_by` must RESOLVE: the named file must ship in the foundation, and when it names a `governance/` or `schemas/` JSON it must carry a `#<dot.path>` anchor that resolves to a real entry in that file — a bare pillar name asserts governance no reader can check, which is how a row can claim a matcher that does not exist. Parity is asserted by internal/tests/ac-191-governance-matrix-parity.sh: a contract key that is neither a `types` entry nor dispositioned here FAILS, and so does a disposition row whose `governed_by` or `registered_type` does not resolve. Adding a contract file requires adding its `types` entry OR its disposition row in the same change.

_index.rationale: Not unregistered — the contract file is named for the FILE (`_index.md`) while the type it governs is `index`, which IS a `types` entry with a required-field set. The contract self-declares the mapping in its own `frontmatter_contract_source`, and governance/mandatory-files-rules.json#mandates._index_md binds the same pair.

adr.rationale: Plan-tree decision records live outside the vault-resident note surface and are governed by the plans pillar (filename_pattern + status_enum + required_sections) plus the manifest pointer array in schemas/plan-manifest-schema.json#decision_records[]. The real renderer is skills/librarian/capabilities/plan-decision-log.sh; the contract's own `_design_notes` naming plan-index is a misnomer (plan-index carries no ADR handling).

doc-amender-prompt.rationale: Operator-authored prompt assets live OUTSIDE the vault in the writer state root, so the vault-scoped R-32 required-field DENY cannot reach them by construction. NO pillar or schema matcher governs them: the contract is SELF-declaring — it carries its own frontmatter_required/frontmatter_optional/frontmatter_enums — and is read directly by its runtime consumers, skills/doc-amender/process.sh and skills/govern/modes/doc-amender-prompt.sh.

episodic-chronicle.rationale: The curated episodic tier lives in the per-project memory directory, outside the vault, and its row shape is declared by the memory schema. The contract's append-only/newest-first fields are convention prose naming no write-time enforcer; its consumers are skills/librarian/capabilities/chronicle-index.sh and the session episode writer.

handoff.rationale: A plan-tree quartet member governed by the plans pillar. Its BODY shape is the enforced surface — hooks/pre-write-guard.sh reads this contract's section_schema for a write-time DENY on a malformed session heading — not a frontmatter required-field set. The renderer is skills/librarian/capabilities/plan-handoff-index.sh; the contract's own `_design_notes` naming plan-index is a misnomer (plan-index carries no handoff handling). The append-only claim in the same contract names no enforcer.

library-article.rationale: Not unregistered — the contract file is named for the ARTIFACT (a library article) while the type it governs is `reference`, which IS a `types` entry with a required-field set. The contract itself declares `type: reference`. Its size_limits are enforced audit-time by skills/librarian/capabilities/library-index.sh, which the contract states honestly.

manifest.rationale: The governed file is JSON and carries no YAML frontmatter at all, so a frontmatter `types` entry has nothing to key on. Full validation delegates to schemas/plan-manifest-schema.json (conditional-on-status). The contract's prose_prohibited rule names no enforcer in the runtime.

spec.rationale: A plan-tree quartet member governed by the plans pillar. Its contract's frontmatter_required_hints are prose-annotated HINTS (e.g. `parent_plan (depth >= 3)`), not machine-consumable field tokens, and its head_immutable_sections claim names no enforcer in the runtime. Registering the type here would retro-fire a required-field DENY across an existing plan corpus authored before any such contract.

tasks.rationale: A plan-tree quartet member governed by the plans pillar. The enforced surface is the ledger-plus-per-task BODY shape rendered by skills/librarian/capabilities/tasks-render.sh in lockstep with manifest.tasks[], not a frontmatter required-field set; the contract's own `_design_notes` naming plan-index is a misnomer (plan-index carries no tasks handling).

path_routing._description: Cross-cutting folder-lineage validation rules (absorbed from vault-schema._path_rules; renamed for clarity). Hook contract: when a file is written, evaluate matching path rules; if pattern matches, the file MUST satisfy the requires_fields + requires_tags clauses. Foundation ships an EMPTY rules[] array — archetype-specific folder patterns belong to adopter overlay-master.frontmatter.path_routing.rules[], not foundation governance. Onboarding wizard offers archetype seeds at install time and writes the adopter's selection into overlay-master. Foundation declares the SHAPE (rules[] array contract + per-rule field semantics via _rule_shape_contract below); adopter provides the CONTENT.

_rule_shape_contract._description: Per-rule object shape that adopter overlay-master.frontmatter.path_routing.rules[] entries MUST conform to. Reference contract for the wizard (onboarding successor) when authoring lineage rules into overlay-master at install time.
exemptions: <file-path patterns that bypass this rule (e.g., folder-level navigation/index files)>
_rule_shape_contract.pattern: <glob path with {placeholder} segments for field-bound depth markers>

property_types._description: Value-type declarations for the universal typed cohort, consumed write-time by pre-write-guard.sh's R-64 property-typing format-regex branch (Tier 1 advisory; warn-not-DENY under the shipped default). date = ^YYYY-MM-DD; list = a YAML sequence; slug-string = ^[a-z0-9]+(-[a-z0-9]+)*$; int = ^[0-9]+$. Mirrored (UX-only) into a seeded .obsidian/types.json — brain-stem can seed but cannot enforce Obsidian's own property types; the enforceable layer is this format regex.

retired_types._description: Types removed from the active type registry; preserved for write-time DENY messaging (R-32 retired_types_handling). Absorbed from vault-schema._retired_types; replacement text abstracted off user-vocabulary folder names — concrete adopter folder patterns live in overlay-master.frontmatter.path_routing.rules[].

engagement.reason: Type information lives at file level only — folders don't have frontmatter. `engagement` is NOT a canonical TYPE; it is a FIELD slot that propagates folder lineage to files. Folders own structural artifact; field + tag propagate to file level.
engagement.replacement: Use `engagement: <slug>` as FIELD on any file living under the adopter's engagement-archetype lineage folder. Foundation declares the field; adopter's overlay-master.frontmatter.path_routing.rules[] declares the lineage glob (consultant archetype seed or extension). For the engagement-level navigation file itself, use type=`navigation`.

project.reason: Same as `engagement` — folders own project lineage; FIELD `project` propagates lineage to files.
project.replacement: Use `project: <slug>` as FIELD on any file living under the adopter's project sub-cluster lineage folder. Foundation declares the field; adopter's overlay-master.frontmatter.path_routing.rules[] declares the lineage glob. For the project-level overview file itself, use type=`context` or type=`navigation` (per file purpose).

system-governance-spoke.reason: Retired type — the foundation no longer ships in-vault narrative spokes; the governance pillar content is published in the hosted docs instead. A file declaring this type is editing a legacy spoke that is now ordinary user-owned content carrying no foundation contract.
system-governance-spoke.replacement: No replacement type. The file is now plain user content; choose an active type that fits its purpose (e.g. type=`navigation` for a folder overview, type=`reference` for a knowledge article), or leave it untracked. The governance narrative it mirrored lives in the hosted docs, not an in-vault spoke.

tier_compliance._description: Canonical three-tier compliance definitions (absorbed from dissolved vault-schema.json `tiers` block; this pillar is now the single source of truth for tier semantics + enforcement metadata).

minimal.applies_to: files matching minimal_tier_exemptions glob patterns OR carrying explicit `tier: minimal` frontmatter directive
minimal.description: Explicit opt-out files. No validation; flagged 'outside system' by librarian. Used for legacy imports, paste-buffer scratch, archives outside lifecycle.

standard.applies_to: type entries with tier=standard in this pillar's `types` block
standard.description: User-authored vault content. Soft warning; librarian flags drift via tag-coverage-audit + frontmatter-coverage-audit capabilities.

strict.applies_to: type entries with tier=strict in this pillar's `types` block
strict.description: System files (scaffold-emitted, /ingest-routed, scraper-aggregated to Inbox/). Hard fail at write-time (R-32 Tier 2 DENY).

types._description: Canonical type registry — the foundation-shipped vault-side type entries plus retired_types reference. Each entry declares tier + per-type required + optional + conditional_required + (optional) body_structure_contract + canonical_scope (provides-presence advisory membership) + (optional) expected_path (folder-placement advisory; array of {pattern, label} per type). Adopters extend the registry via overlay-master.frontmatter.types[] (registered via `/govern register --kind file-type`) — ADD a new type, or SUPERSEDE a shipped one with a FULL replacement entry carrying `_override_reason` (R-52). A `null` overlay entry is NOT a delete and is rejected at load; there is no adopter-facing NULLIFY. Plan-tree types (spec, tasks, handoff) are governed by the plans pillar, not registered here; every file-type contract whose key is not an entry in this registry carries an explicit disposition in `file_type_contract_dispositions`.

deliverable._description: Durable, human/agent-authored work product under the Work/ surface (Work/<spoke>/deliverables/<name>.md) — the durable + human-authored context surface. Lifecycle frontmatter (status, audience) and enums are governed by governance/file-type-contracts/deliverable.md.json; the body is free-form because deliverables are heterogeneous. Enforcement fires at BOTH layers: write-time on REGISTERED-spoke Work/ writes — the pre-write-guard.sh remap prelude rewrites a registered Work/<spoke>/ write onto the vault path BEFORE the 3-tier schema block, so the write IS governed — with the librarian suite over the Work/ symlink view as the audit-time backstop for everything else (unregistered spokes, hand-authored files reached via the scoped symlink walk). A deliverable is never machine-written; the bounded exception is the sentinel-bounded generated files (the work-side directory map + the work-subfolder _index.md navigation files), a disjoint artifact class that is out of the deliverable contract. `expected_path` (Work/**) is an audit-time placement advisory, not a write-time matcher.

ideation-brief._description: Plan-tree ideation brief files at ~/.claude-plans/<plan>/00-ideation-brief.md. Validated against this type registry as an interim measure; planned relocation to plans pillar type registry as a follow-up.

parent_folder.condition_semantics: depth is the number of path segments between the vault root and the file; depth 1 = `<cluster>/_index.md` (parent_folder omitted because the parent IS the vault root); depth >= 2 = `<cluster>/<instance>/_index.md` or deeper (parent_folder mandatory).

Clause (a) excludes standard [filename](memory/..) index entries that merely mention ~/ or /Users in their description text.

_memory_md_cap.rationale: Anthropic-documented at code.claude.com/docs/en/memory: the first 200 lines of MEMORY.md, or the first 25,000 UTF-16 code units of the trimmed, frontmatter- and comment-stripped text, whichever comes first, are loaded at the start of every conversation. Entries past the cap are dropped and the harness announces it, appending a model-visible WARNING footer naming the overflow to the content it did load. The advisory makes the same risk visible one step earlier, at write-time, before the index is saved. MEMORY.md = index/read-replica; per-topic detail lives in memory/<file>.md reached via index-entry links and [[wikilink]] cross-references — the memory/rules pointer tier is EXEMPT from the corpus link-grammar conversion (its links resolve against the enumerated memory namespace, not the vault walk). The byte cap is the governing trigger (bites at ~110 entries before the line cap).

_rules._enforcement_scope_depth3_note: The last two globs ({plans_root}/*/*/spec.md + {plans_root}/*/*/manifest.json) extend R-27's enforcement to depth-3 sub-plan roots. A depth-3 sub-plan manifest.json is a governed peer carrying its OWN canonical status, NOT a status-derived shadow of the master; a sub-plan can be paused independently of its master, and the master sub_plans[] aggregate reflects each sub's published status. A depth-3 sub-plan spec.md is manifest-derived under the single status SoT — it defers to its sibling manifest's status rather than carrying its own. The hook substance asserts: (a) parent dir matches {plans_root}/NN-{master}/NN-{sub}/; (b) target is spec.md or manifest.json; (c) for manifest.json, status: present + value in the lifecycle.status_enum; (d) for spec.md, an inline **Status:**/YAML status: OR a sibling manifest.json status — DENY fires only when neither an inline marker nor a sibling-manifest status is present.
_rules.failure_mode: Plans without numeric prefix or status break librarian plan-index regeneration. Shame slugs degrade plan-index, backlog routing, and search-by-name.
_rules.rule_text: New or edited plan-root files must carry (a) an `NN-` numeric prefix on their top-level path segment AND (b) an authoritative status. The status is satisfied by any of: a `**Status:**` header bullet, YAML `status:` frontmatter, a `manifest.json` top-level `status` field, OR — for `spec.md` and `00-ideation-brief.md` — a sibling `manifest.json` carrying a top-level `status` field. spec.md/00-ideation-brief.md are manifest-derived: the manifest is the single status SoT, so an artifact carrying no inline status defers to its plan's manifest and DENYs only when the manifest carries no status either. Flat-root plans and README.md have no sibling manifest and keep the inline `**Status:**`/`status:` requirement; a `manifest.json` write keeps its OWN top-level `status`. Status values use the canonical 6-state lifecycle.status_enum; the spec-status-enum advisory rides inside R-27 (advisory; never retro-denies legacy plans). Sub-task files, handoffs, and orchestrator artifacts inherit from parent per R-28 and are NOT required to carry status. DENY at write-time.

_rules.rule_text: Sub-publishes-upward: a sub-plan publishes its status + graduation_timestamp upward to the master (the master reads them into sub_plans[]); a sub MUST NOT mutate the master aggregate directly. Cross-file invariant enforced by the librarian reconciler (NOT write-time).

_rules.failure_mode: A sub declares a direct dependency on a sibling sub, recreating the agent-teams peer model the orchestrator-worker model deliberately rejects (MAST coordination-failure class). Advisory drift finding at session-close.
_rules.rule_text: Sub-peer-isolation: a sub-plan manifest MUST NOT carry a dependencies edge to a sibling sub-plan — route through the master manifest (the orchestrator-worker invariant: workers report only to the orchestrator, never to each other). Surfaced as a librarian reconciler drift finding (advisory).

_rules.legacy_label_note: RENAME COMPLETED: the guard block's emitted advisory strings historically carried '[R-40 PLAN FRONTMATTER]' (and sibling [R-40 LIBRARY/BINDER]) prefixes — a label collision, since the bare R-40 id is owned by the frontmatter pillar's provides-canonicality rule. _rules.rule_text: The 5 canonical Markdown plan artifacts must carry the canonical type: for their basename (spec.md -> spec, tasks.md -> tasks, handoff.md -> handoff, 00-ideation-brief.md -> ideation-brief, traceability-matrix.md -> traceability-matrix) per schemas/plans-schema.json. (2) Inbox idea notes carry inbox.funnel_status_enum {new, triaged, briefed} — a DIFFERENT object type (a pre-plan idea note, not a plan manifest), NOT collapsed into the 6-state plan status. The inbox funnel is separate from the plan-status enum. backlog_row.status_enum is the documented union shown in the rendered _backlog.md view.

backlog_row._stale_advisory_days_note: [advisory_threshold, escalation_threshold] in days for a backlog row missing a disposition. backlog-index emits backlog-row-missing-disposition once per run; backlog-hygiene escalates severity Warning->Alert by stale_for_days against these thresholds (R-56).

settled_section._note: Derived settled ledger rendered below the active table by librarian:backlog-index — THREE sources: graduated items joined from plan manifests' promoted_from, absorption joins from plan manifests' absorbed_notes[] (one row per listed note, landing plan named; a note-side row for the same note takes precedence), and inbox notes carrying a terminal resolution (flat or in the settled home); never hand-kept.

decision_records._description: Per-plan ADR (Architecture Decision Record) ledger. Short, immutable, individually-addressable, supersession-tracked decision records. Optional: a plan with no recorded decisions has no decisions/ dir. Body-structure contract at governance/file-type-contracts/adr.md.json; manifest pointer array at schemas/plan-manifest-schema.json :: decision_records[].
decision_records.agent_reload_contract: On plan resume, load non-superseded ADRs via manifest.decision_records[] as the decision context — NOT spec-prose archaeology.
decision_records.immutability: An accepted ADR is immutable. A decision change creates a NEW ADR that supersedes the prior one (prior Status -> superseded-by-ADR-NN); never an in-place edit. Distinct from the spec.md append-amendment pattern.
decision_records.placement_rule: repo-tier (docs/decisions/, 4-digit) IFF the decision changes adopter-inherited foundation behavior; else plan-tier (<plan>/decisions/ADR-NN-<slug>.md, 2-digit).
decision_records.tooling: NONE (no adr-tools / log4brains). Markdown-in-git + librarian enumeration covers it; bundling violates minimum-viable.

inbox._description: Pre-plan idea capture surface. Lightweight per-idea notes at ~/.claude-plans/_inbox/<slug>.md — cheap capture, extended-form body that grows in place, hook-unblocked (hooks/lib/plan-path.sh::classify_plan_path returns is_plan=0 so R-27 prefix/status never fires). Rendered into the unified _backlog.md by librarian:backlog-index. Graduates to a full plan via the idea->plan promote path (migrates body -> 00-ideation-brief.md, scaffolds the NN- quartet, tombstones the note).
inbox._slug_pattern_note: Inbox notes have NO NN- numeric prefix (distinct from plan slugs). The prefix is assigned at graduation, not at capture — avoids prefix burn on discarded ideas.
inbox.body: free-form extended idea content (description / rationale / notes); grows in place across funnel stages until graduation

lifecycle._description: ONE canonical 6-state plan `status`. The single authoritative `status` lives on schemas/plan-manifest-schema.json :: status; this block declares the transition gates the librarian reconciler enforces. completed is the sole terminal done-state; archival is a display-only view filter over completed plans, never a status.

in-progress->completed._note: completed = the human's claim that work is done; the sole terminal done-state

root_namespace._description: CLOSED plans-root namespace. The plans-tree root admits ONLY the entry classes enumerated in allowed_entry_classes — nothing else. This is the single source of truth read by the write-time root-allowlist guard (hooks/pre-write-guard.sh, positioned before R-27), the sweep-side rule (skills/librarian/capabilities/placement-validate.sh), and the shared classifier hooks/lib/plan-path.sh::classify_root_entry. A root entry matching no allowed class is non-conforming: ask->deny at write-time (advisory-to-blocking rollout), flagged by the sweep. Rationale: session outputs with no owning plan otherwise invent root surfaces whose records get no lifecycle; a closed namespace routes durable artifacts to their owning context instead.

dot_entries._description: Leading-dot entries (.git, .gitignore, .DS_Store, .active-plan, dotfiles) are class-exempt so the closed namespace does not fight VCS/OS/pointer machinery.

funnel_registry_surfaces._description: Enumerated funnel + registry directories: _inbox (pre-plan idea capture), _projects (per-spoke binder registry), _library (universal-only cross-project library). Historical registry documents are deliberately NOT enumerated surfaces — the governance JSON pillar is the live rule source of truth, and a historical map file is not a durable root registry.

legacy_flat_plans._description: Depth-1 flat NN-<slug>.md plans — kept in place, not retroactively invalidated (each carries inbound citations). CLOSED class: the scaffolder mints directories only, so no new flat-plan members can appear through the sanctioned path.

plan_dirs._description: NN-<slug> plan directories (conforming-active; R-27-governed prefix + status).

root_files._description: Librarian-generated root registry files (also enumerated under root_files above).

metadata_flow._description: Orchestrator-worker contract for first-class master/sub-plan structure. Maps onto Claude Code's subagent orchestrator-worker invariant: workers run in isolated contexts, report only to the orchestrator, and NEVER communicate with each other — the deliberate OPPOSITE of the agent-teams peer model. Master/sub aggregation is pull-based and DERIVED: the master sub_plans[] is a librarian-generated read-replica (same trust class as _index.md), NEVER hand-edited.
metadata_flow.aggregation_model: pull-based-derived-read-replica (librarian reconciler reads each sub's published status into the master's sub_plans[]; never hand-edited; same class as _index.md)
parent_plan_exempt_files: Plan-root files at depth 2 (spec.md, tasks.md, handoff.md, 00-ideation-brief.md, README.md, manifest.json) — they ARE the parent
handoff.md at any depth (append-only session record)

tagging._description: Pillar 2 — Tagging (per-pillar rule model). Loaded by pre-write-guard.sh at runtime. Homes R-05 (deny, tag-validation), R-47 (advisory, tag-presence), R-50 (advisory, 25-tag cap). The R-60 (deny, tag grammar) _rules[] OBJECT is homed in governance/naming-rules.json — it appears in the tagging rule_id_range (category=tagging) only, NOT duplicated here. _rules[] is the per-pillar rule SoT (each object carries home/category/surface?/status). Carries the canonical tag-prefix taxonomy. Tags are the user-side query surface (Obsidian graph view, filter pane, MOC patterns); frontmatter fields are the Claude-side substrate.

_design_notes.consumer: pre-write-guard.sh — tag-validation branch (R-05) + tag-presence advisory (R-47); librarian tag-coverage-audit (R-47, R-50); onboarder consolidation prompt (R-50, install-time)
_design_notes.evolution_protocol: R-37 documentary lockstep — tagging-rules.json + pre-write-guard.sh tag-validation branch move in one commit (the r37_coupled_surfaces set declared at governance/_index.json#pillars[tagging]). NO write-time DENY for R-37, by design (R-37 is documentary across the governance surface — git commit-boundary atomicity + librarian governance-parity-audit at session-close; a PreToolUse hook sees exactly one file per call and cannot inspect a multi-file commit set).
_design_notes.rule_id_range_reconciliation: _index.json#pillars[tagging].rule_id_range = [R-05, R-60, R-47, R-50]. This pillar's _rules[] = [R-05, R-47, R-50] (3 objects). R-60 is in the range (its tag-grammar substance is category=tagging) but its _rules[] object is HOMED in governance/naming-rules.json. This is the home != range divergence — the tagging surface owns R-60's runtime substance (it validates against this pillar's taxonomy); naming owns R-60's declaration site.

enforcement_layer: pre-write-guard.sh tag-validation branch (system-utility dimension DENY on near-match)
_rules.failure_mode: Near-match drift in system-utility dimensions fragments operational subtypes within weeks. Two runs of the same routine emit two different tag values (e.g., #log/backlog-hygiene vs #log/backlog-cleanup), and the user-side graph filter splits routine activity across variant spellings. The discipline restores stability: every routine activity uses the STABLE, canonical tag value registered at first emission, and the hook DENIES near-match drift.
_rules.rule_text: Tags within system-utility dimensions (#log/*, #status/*) must match a value registered in governance/log-subtype-registry.json. Near-match writes (Levenshtein distance <= 2 or substring containment of an existing canonical value) are DENIED with a 'did you mean #<dim>/<canonical>?' suggestion. Genuinely new subtypes register explicitly via the prompt-and-commit pattern at first emission. The discipline mirrors the canonical-tag-per-concept principle on the system-utility surface where LLM stochasticity would otherwise fragment the vocabulary.

_rules.exempt_path_semantics: positive-list — unenumerated top-level paths default to the advisory firing (NOT auto-exempt). Adding a new exempt path requires R-37 documentary lockstep updating this rule + pre-write-guard.sh + foundation-master.json bundle composition (composed via tools/build-foundation-master.sh, never hand-edited).
_rules.failure_mode: Non-exempt files written without tags become orphans in Obsidian graph view — invisible to user-side queries even though the file is legible to Claude-side surfaces via frontmatter fields. Pre-write tag-presence advisory surfaces the omission at the moment of write rather than at the weekly audit, closing a ~7-day detection lag.
_rules.rule_text: Every non-exempt vault write MUST carry a non-empty `tags:` array in its frontmatter. Pre-write-guard emits a Tier 1 advisory ([R-47 TAG PRESENCE]) when the field is missing or empty (tags: []). Distinguishes 'missing' (no tags: line) vs 'empty' (line present, no items). Exempt paths are enumerated in this rule's `r47_exempt_paths` array — they cover archive surfaces, ideation-brief symlinks, machine-emitted scratch/build zones, and system infrastructure paths whose tag-absence is structurally legitimate. The librarian tag-coverage-audit walks the vault at audit time and surfaces longer-running orphans + near-miss patterns (#scope/decisions vs #scope/decision — one is likely a typo) as advisory findings the operator triages.
_rules.seed_taxonomy_exempt_paths_semantics: DEDICATED tag-TAXONOMY exempt-list — SEPARATE from r47_exempt_paths (which is the tag-PRESENCE exempt-list for R-47). The foundation seeds #vault-writers on Vault Writers/_index.md to model good tagging for adopters; the foundation taxonomy ships NO vault-writers dimension (its user-facing dimension set is project-only — taxonomy.user_facing_dimensions), so that seed tag is NOT a member of the foundation allowlist and the tag-taxonomy membership arm would flag it. This one glob surface exempts EXACTLY that seed from the tag-not-in-taxonomy membership check ONLY — the seed stays byte-unchanged, still obeys the R-47 tag-PRESENCE rule (r47_exempt_paths untouched), and adopter-authored tags on non-exempt paths are unaffected. Composed deterministically to foundation-master.json#seed_taxonomy_exempt_paths_composed via tools/build-foundation-master.sh (never hand-edit the bundle).

enforcement_layer: librarian tag-coverage-audit (audit-time consolidation prompt at 80% threshold)
documentary in the hosted governance docs (vault-governance.md)
_rules.failure_mode: Cap-widening defeats the working-memory rationale silently. An adopter activates a new engagement, user-facing tag count approaches 25, and the path of least resistance is 'raise the cap to 30.' Past 25, decision fatigue produces variant-creation rather than canonical-term selection, the vocabulary fragments, and user-side recall collapses. The cap is structural, not aspirational — silent widening is rejected; deliberate Layer 3 override is supported with audit trail.
_rules.override_mechanism: Layer 3 overlay-master.json :: tagging_cap_override with rationale + audit-trail entry
_rules.rule_text: Total count of distinct values across user-facing dimensions (declared at runtime by union of foundation-master.tagging.taxonomy.user_facing_dimensions + overlay-master.tagging.taxonomy.user_facing_dimensions) MUST stay under 25. System-utility dimensions (log, status) are exempt — they are machine-emitted and governed by the log-subtype registry (R-05). The librarian tag-coverage-audit emits an advisory when user-facing usage approaches 80% of the cap (>= 20 active values), surfaces a consolidation prompt with retire-candidate recommendations, and requires deliberate Layer 3 override (`overlay-master.json :: tagging_cap_override` with rationale + audit-trail entry) before silent widening can proceed.
_rules.source: governance/tagging-rules.json :: _rules (SoT; 25-tag cap grounded in Forte/Dubois working-vocabulary research + Hedden faceted-classification literature + Adobe AEM and SharePoint enterprise CMS picklist patterns)

taxonomy._description: Faceted tag taxonomy (canonical authority). Foundation ships taxonomy SHAPE + the system-utility dimensions (status, log — governed by log-subtype-registry — plus the generator-stamped episode and scope, which mark durable session records and generated/writer pages respectively and carry no canonical-value registry) + the user-facing dimensions: project (see _project_dimension_note) and library (#library/<topic> — topic navigation over authored library articles; topic slugs are identifiers, not vocabulary terms). Additional user-facing dimensions belong to the adopter overlay — overlay-master.tagging.taxonomy.dimension_prefixes + .user_facing_dimensions — populated by the adopter's onboarding/extension flow. Runtime allowlist = the read-time foundation+overlay union (see _runtime_allowlist_resolution).
taxonomy._runtime_allowlist_resolution: hooks/lib/foundation-overlay-load.sh produces the read-time union view: hooks/lib/merge-strategy-registry.json declares tagging.taxonomy.dimension_prefixes and tagging.taxonomy.user_facing_dimensions as union leaves, and the loader emits an order-preserving concat+dedup of foundation-master + overlay-master values for each (payload-replace applies only to non-union leaves). Consumers read the UNION view, never a single bundle — pre-write-guard.sh's tag-taxonomy branch derives its prefix allowlist (R32_TAXONOMY_UNION_PREFIXES) from it, falling back to the foundation-only set when no overlay is present. foundation-master.json composes the foundation side from this pillar; the adopter overlay extends it.
taxonomy.canonical_authority: governance/tagging-rules.json#taxonomy (the dissolved-schema anchors _tag_prefixes / _tag_prefixes_meta resolve to dimension_prefixes / (system_utility_dimensions + user_facing_dimensions + cap_25_applies_to) here)
taxonomy.system_utility_governance: log-subtype-registry (canonical values per dimension; near-match DENY via R-05)
